cards.title: Google DeepMind Launches Multilingual Sign-Language-to-Text Model, Deploys in Gboard and Live Transcribe
cards.why_it_matters: This is a meaningful multimodal ML milestone—training on 100K+ hours across 50+ sign languages with a pose-landmark input pipeline rather than raw video is a notable architecture and data-scaling decision worth tracking.
cards.summary: DeepMind's SL2T model is trained on over 100,000 hours of data across more than 50 sign languages, using on-device MediaPipe Holistic pose landmarks (not raw video) to protect privacy. Joint multilingual training outperformed single-language models in experiments. SL2T now powers ASL-to-English sign-to-text dictation in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11, with more devices and languages planned.

cards.title: LLMs Still Struggle at Long-Form Non-Fiction: A Textbook Author's Assessment
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/research engineer, this practitioner-level critique of LLM writing limitations from someone who just authored a post-training/RLHF textbook offers a grounded counterweight to hype about AI-driven autonomous science.
cards.summary: Nathan Lambert, having used LLMs extensively while writing an RLHF textbook, argues models have stagnated at organizing and compellingly presenting established knowledge in long-form non-fiction—despite leaping from weak to superhuman at coding and math. He contends this knowledge-compression failure is a prerequisite gap before LLMs can autonomously solve open science problems, limiting near-term AI science progress to low-hanging fruit and cross-field connection rather than genuine insight.

cards.title: AVA-Encoder: Video-to-Knowledge-Graph Auto-Encoding for Agent-Native Video Representations
cards.why_it_matters: Representing video as an editable knowledge graph with typed edges that agents can query and manipulate is a technically interesting approach to bridging video understanding and agentic reasoning pipelines.
cards.summary: AVA-Encoder encodes video into a knowledge graph with hierarchy/state text nodes and a linked asset layer (images, audio, video clips), then reconstructs video from it. Reconstruction error drives textual-gradient optimization via pseudo-training in an outer loop and optional test-time KG refinement. The method reports a 20.7 percentage-point improvement over the strongest external baseline, and its pseudo-trained shot-level encoder policy uses 74.3% fewer system-prompt tokens than a human-tuned policy.

cards.title: DreamFly: Causal Memory and Receding-Horizon Diffusion Planning for Aerial VLN
cards.why_it_matters: The receding-horizon diffusion planning design—predict K-step action chunk, execute only the first, then replan—is a clean architectural pattern relevant to anyone working on embodied agents or long-horizon action generation.
cards.summary: DreamFly addresses aerial vision-language navigation with three components: causally aligned historical memory (uses only past observations), receding-horizon diffusion planning (predict K steps, execute one), and LiteStop (estimates stop probability from action logits at the initial all-mask state). On the OpenFly benchmark, it achieves 32.04%/29.46% success rate and 28.22%/23.54% SPL on test-seen/test-unseen splits, outperforming all compared methods on both metrics.

cards.title: Strong-to-Weak Test-Time Capability Transfer: Harnesses Nearly Double Weaker Model Performance on ToM Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: Showing that a stronger model can construct inference-time scaffolds that boost a weaker model from 0.49 to 0.91 average accuracy—without any parameter updates—is directly relevant to deployment strategies and complements distillation research.
cards.summary: The paper tests whether a stronger 'builder' model can iteratively construct inference-time harnesses (code offloading, benchmark-specific routing, strict answer-format enforcement) that lift a weaker 'target' model on Theory-of-Mind benchmarks, using 5% of data for harness refinement. Average target performance nearly doubles from 0.49 to 0.91. Gains come primarily from deterministic code offloading rather than extended reasoning, and weaker targets benefit most.

cards.title: RCI Framework: Converting Sparse Stop-Feedback into Dense Costs for Safe Offline RL
cards.why_it_matters: Addressing the realistic sparse-label setting for safe RL—where only a binary stop signal is available rather than per-step cost annotations—via return decomposition is a practically important contribution for anyone building constrained offline RL systems.
cards.summary: RCI (Redistribution-based Cost Inference) takes binary trajectory-level stop-feedback and uses return decomposition to redistribute it into dense per-step cost signals, then trains a constrained offline policy on the augmented dataset in a CMDP framework. The paper proves return-equivalent redistribution preserves the feasible policy set and optimal Lagrangian. Experiments on highway driving and robotic manipulation show substantially lower violation rates versus sparse and classifier-based baselines, with robustness to label noise.

cards.title: OlmoEarth Studio Now Exports Custom Geospatial Embedding Vectors for Downstream ML
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on geospatial or environmental ML, this open-weight foundation model with exportable embeddings at multiple resolutions and encoder sizes is a ready-to-use building block for similarity search, segmentation, and change detection pipelines.
cards.summary: OlmoEarth Studio can now compute and export embedding vectors from its open-source Earth-observation foundation models as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs. Users choose area, time range (1–12 monthly periods), encoder variant (Nano 128-dim/1.4M params, Tiny 192-dim/6.2M params, or Base 768-dim/89M params), resolution (10–80 m/pixel), and imagery source (Sentinel-2 L2A, Sentinel-1 RTC, or both). Vectors are stored as int8; model weights and code are publicly available.

cards.title: LiquidAI Releases LFM2.5-VL-3B: Fast Edge VLM with RL Post-Training and 11K tok/s GPU Throughput
cards.why_it_matters: A 3B-class VLM hitting ~11K tokens/second at high concurrency on a single H100 and 20 tok/s on a Galaxy S26 Ultra, with RL-based post-training and strong tool-use, is a practically significant edge-deployment result.
cards.summary: LFM2.5-VL-3B pairs a SigLIP2 400M NaFlex vision encoder with a 2.6B text backbone pretrained on ~34T tokens. Post-training uses SFT with knowledge distillation plus multi-reward RL. The model achieves ~11K tokens/second throughput at high concurrency on an H100 (roughly 2× larger 4B-class models), 228 tok/s on an M5 Max, and fits in ~3 GB. Tool-use performance matches Gemma-4-E2B and Qwen3.5-2B; tokenizer vocabulary doubled to 128K for non-Latin script support.
